description:
We are a team passionate about technology, innovation, and solving real-world challenges. Our project, Field Shift, aims to transform NASA Earth observation data into practical agricultural insights.

We are building an intelligent crop rotation decision-support platform that helps farmers understand environmental conditions, evaluate crop rotation strategies, and make more informed decisions about soil health, water availability, and climate challenges.
summary:
Field Shift – Adapting Farms with NASA Data

Farmers around the world are facing shifting temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, water shortages, extreme weather, and declining soil health. These pressures make it difficult to choose crop rotations that protect fields, conserve water, and support long-term resilience.

Our project addresses this challenge by developing a decision-support tool that helps farmers explore crop rotation strategies tailored to their conditions. The tool combines four inputs:

NASA Earth observations, such as temperature, precipitation, and soil moisture data
Local soil information
Crop characteristics, such as water demand, root depth, and nitrogen-fixing ability
Farmer priorities, such as profit, water conservation, and soil health

Using these inputs, the tool generates and compares rotation strategies, presents the results through clear visualizations, and explains why each option suits the farmer’s context. The goal is to strengthen soil health and help farms adapt to changing conditions while keeping the decision in the farmer’s hands.
details:
What it does and how it works
Field Shift is a decision-support tool that helps farmers explore crop rotation strategies that strengthen soil health and adapt their farms to changing conditions. The farmer enters their location, local soil type, the crops they grow, and their priorities (such as profit, water conservation, or soil health). The tool retrieves NASA Earth observation data, including temperature and rainfall (NASA POWER), soil moisture (SMAP), and vegetation health (MODIS). It combines this data with crop characteristics such as water demand, root depth, and nitrogen-fixing ability. It then scores and compares multiple rotation plans, shows the results in clear visual charts, and explains in plain language why each plan suits the farmer’s situation.

Benefits
Farmers get a clear, data-backed way to compare rotation options instead of relying on guesswork. Plans can reduce water use, rebuild soil nutrients, and lower the risk from extreme weather, while still respecting the farmer’s own goals.

Intended impact
Our goal is healthier soil, more efficient water use, and more resilient farms over the long term. By turning free NASA open data into simple recommendations, Field Shift makes climate-adaptive farming accessible to farmers who do not have access to expensive advisory services.

Tools and technologies
[List what you used, e.g. HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, charting library, NASA POWER API, SMAP and MODIS data, GitHub for hosting.]

Creativity
Field Shift turns complex satellite data into a simple, visual experience. Instead of showing raw numbers, it compares rotation plans side by side and explains the reasoning in everyday language. It also keeps the farmer in control of the final decision, since each farmer can set their own priorities.

Factors we considered
We considered differences in local climate and soil, trade-offs between profit, water use, and soil health, the needs of farmers with limited technical experience, and the reliability and availability of NASA data. We designed the interface to be simple, visual, and easy to use.
